flags.title: No Las Vegas Strip event is published as a true freezeout
flags.detail: Across all 37 Venetian structure sheets and every Wynn terms sheet that the WPT posted, not one event states “no re-entry” or “freezeout”. Two Venetian events are explicitly re-entry-priced (#18, #58: “All subsequent buy in's after the initial buy in will be $200”) and every Wynn event with a terms sheet states unlimited re-entry. The strict single-entry list is therefore empty of confirmed rows, and every candidate is shown as unverified rather than promoted.
flags.action: Ask each poker room, in writing, whether the event is a freezeout. Until an official page says so, treat “unverified” rows as possibly re-entry.

flags.title: The 8:00 a.m. start goal cannot be met on the Strip
flags.detail: Earliest official start found: Venetian 9:10 a.m. (event #46, Dec 12) and Venetian 10:10 a.m. for the regular slate; Wynn 10:00 a.m. (Super Gold Million, Dec 10–11); Horseshoe 9:00 a.m. (daily, per Caesars' own article). Nothing on an official page starts at 8:00 a.m.
flags.action: Either accept a 9:10 a.m. first start or add an off-Strip room with a pre-9 a.m. start once verified.

flags.title: Bellagio weekly event carries three different buy-ins in one PDF
flags.detail: The Bellagio Saturday PDF is titled “NLH $1100 BUY-IN”, is linked from the poker page as “SATURDAYS | $1,000 NLH”, and rule 07 says “Of the $600 Buy-in, $510 goes to the Prize Pool”. The same sheet has stale dates (Day 2 “9/13/26”), so the sheet appears to be an un-updated template.
flags.action: Confirm the actual Saturday buy-in with the Bellagio poker room before budgeting.

flags.title: Bellagio's optional $40 gratuity buys 20,000 extra chips
flags.detail: Rule 09: “The voluntary staff gratuity will grant players an extra 20,000 chips.” A $40 payment inside the $600 structure therefore buys a 50% larger starting stack - exactly the pay-for-advantage case the brief wants separated.
flags.action: Keep Bellagio and Caesars out of the strict list; they are documented in the Advantage Events section.

flags.title: Caesars Palace advertises a paid add-on
flags.detail: Caesars' own article: $100 buy-in, 20,000 chips, $1,000 GTD, and “a $50 add-on at the first break gives you an extra 15,000 chips”. No official structure sheet PDF was found, so the level and late-reg details are unverified.
flags.action: Request the official structure sheet; do not budget Caesars until then.

flags.title: Wynn does not publish terms for events after Dec 15
flags.detail: The posted WPT World Championship Structures PDF ends at the $1,600 PLO Mystery Bounty ($500,000 GTD). Entry rules for the $10,400 World Championship, both $10,500 events, the $25,800 High Roller, Seniors, Ladies, Super Gold Million and the $1,000/$2,000/$3,000 NLH events are therefore blank.
flags.action: Re-check wynnpoker.com weekly; Wynn updates the structures link in place.

flags.title: Wynn schedule says World Championship registration stays open into Day 2
flags.detail: The schedule row for Dec 16 reads “WPT World Championship Day 2 (Registration open until the start of Day 2)”. Late registration running into Day 2 is a material difference from a normal freezeout and is recorded as an excerpt, not interpreted.
flags.action: Confirm with Wynn whether a Day-2 entrant pays a fresh $10,400 and starts at a shorter stack.

flags.title: Venetian resort fee is published as “rates include” but the booking engine adds it per night
flags.detail: The resort-fee page says “Rates include a daily Resort Fee of $55 plus tax per night, payable upon check-in”, while the booking breakdown lists $55.00 as a separate line for each night and then applies 13.38% tax on the total.
flags.action: Treat $55 + 13.38% as an unavoidable per-night charge; verify at check-in.

flags.title: LIPS events carry a flat fee that is neither prize pool nor house fee
flags.detail: Structure sheets #31, #32 and #33 add a $10 (or $20 for #39) LIPS fee, so the buy-in does not equal pool plus house fee. The fee is recorded separately and the derived “fee” field is left blank for those events.
flags.action: Budget buy-in + LIPS fee when comparing cost per dollar of prize pool.

flags.title: Venetian multi-flight events are explicitly multi-entry
flags.detail: Sheets #2, #3, #4, #9, #10, #12, #20, #21 and #35 all contain the “bags for Day 2 may not play subsequent flight” rule, which presumes a player can buy into more than one flight.
flags.action: None; they are excluded from the strict list and listed separately.

flags.title: Venetian event #40 row was truncated in the baseline capture - now resolved
flags.detail: Prior flag F02 said event #40's name, time and buy-in were lost. Structure sheet #27 confirms $600 PLO Bounty $25,000 GTD and the schedule shows Dec 10, 12:10 p.m.

flags.title: No official parking or cancellation page retrievable for the Venetian
flags.detail: venetianlasvegas.com/resort/parking.html returns 404 and MGM's parking page also returns 404. Cancellation deadlines are only visible on the rate-rules screen of the booking flow, which is not linkable.
flags.action: Read the rate rules at checkout and screenshot the cancellation deadline.

questions.q: Is each candidate event a freezeout, and can the poker room put that in writing?
questions.why: No official document on the Strip says “no re-entry”, which is the core of the brief. Everything else is a comparison between events that might allow a second buy-in.
questions.how: Email or call the poker room; ask for the event terms, not the marketing page.

questions.q: Does the planned trip include a weekend?
questions.why: Saturday/Sunday carries the biggest guarantees (Wynn $1M flights, Venetian $500K) but also the highest hotel rates - the Venetian night of Dec 5 is $779.25 versus $231.75 on Dec 6.
questions.how: Set exact dates; the calendar grid on the booking engine shows per-night prices before you commit.

questions.q: What is the maximum acceptable cost per tournament hour?
questions.why: A $600 one-day event with 40-minute levels runs roughly 10-12 hours; a $200 turbo runs 5-6. Cost per hour, not buy-in, separates the two.
questions.how: Use the trip calculator on this site and sort by cost per level.

questions.q: Will the player take the Bellagio $40 chip-gratuity or Caesars $50 add-on?
questions.why: Both buy an advantage; if yes, those venues belong in the plan and the strict list must be described as a preference, not a constraint.
questions.how: Decide before comparing; mixing them makes the ranking meaningless.

questions.q: Which hotel tier is required - Venetian suite or a standard Wynn king?
questions.why: Same 7 nights: Venetian $6,927.21 all-in versus Wynn's $711 average room rate before tax. Venetian includes a 650 sq ft suite; Wynn includes self-parking.
questions.how: Book refundable rates on both and compare after tax at checkout.

questions.q: Can a 9:10 a.m. start replace the 8:00 a.m. goal?
questions.why: Nothing on the Strip starts at 8. The earliest verified start is 9:10 a.m.
questions.how: Confirm with the Venetian that event #46's 9:10 a.m. satellite runs on Dec 12, or accept 10:10 a.m.

questions.q: What happens if a day's primary event is a multi-flight bag?
questions.why: Bagging Day 1 forces attendance on Day 2, which can collide with the next day's primary event.
questions.how: Prefer one-day events as primaries and keep flights as conditionals.

questions.q: Is a rental car or rideshare budget needed for Resorts World?
questions.why: Resorts World is 12-18 minutes on foot from Wynn, but nothing else is that close; if the plan expands south, walking stops working.
questions.how: Price a 7-day rideshare estimate and compare with parking fees.

suggestions.title: Publish a per-event cost-per-hour column
suggestions.body: Buy-in alone hides the difference between a 20-minute-level turbo and a 40-minute structure. Deriving hours from levels × level length and dividing buy-in by hours gives a fair comparison. The dashboard already stores level length for every row, so this is a display change only.

suggestions.title: Ask the rooms for written freezeout confirmations in one batch
suggestions.body: A single email template to Venetian, Wynn, Bellagio, Caesars and Resorts World asking “is this event single-entry, and what is the late-registration cut-off” would convert the largest block of unverified rows in one pass.

suggestions.title: Track the Venice/Wynn structure PDFs by checksum
suggestions.body: Both rooms update their structure PDFs in place. The scheduled worker already hashes each URL; surfacing the hash change date next to each event would show exactly when a rule changed.

suggestions.title: Add a like-for-like hotel comparison at one length of stay
suggestions.body: Seven nights, two adults, one room is the current baseline. Adding 3- and 5-night variants at the same check-in date makes the weekend premium visible instead of averaged away.

suggestions.title: Model the bag risk for multi-flight primaries
suggestions.body: If a Day 1 is bagged, the next day is committed. A simple flag that a chosen primary has a Day 2 on the following day would stop the planner proposing an impossible sequence.

suggestions.title: Add an off-Strip section
suggestions.body: The 8 a.m. goal and the no-advantage-purchase rule both point off-Strip, where rooms publish true freezeouts more often. This is the single largest coverage gap.
